title: Key a pulley onto a shaft
instruction: Fit the pulley to the shaft and lock it.
context: Industrial machinery mechanics (SOC 49-9041; 412,650 US jobs), machinery maintenance workers (49-9043; 58,040), millwrights (49-9044; 37,930) and engine and other machine assemblers (51-2031; 47,960), 556,580 in all (BLS OEWS May 2023), fit pulleys, sprockets and couplings to keyed shafts as routine drive assembly and repair. The key has to go into the keyseat first and fully home; a pulley pushed over a loose key cocks it and jams. A set screw that only touches the key lets the pulley walk along the shaft. The instruction does not mention the key, the hex driver or the torque.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the bench top. A bench sub-assembly, not on a machine: no motor or belt is connected, nothing is powered and nothing stores energy; the shaft is clamped so it cannot turn. Shaft: steel, 2 cm diameter, axis along x at y 0, 4 cm up, from x 20.5 (free end) to x 37.5, clamped on a blue support block (3 x 5 x 3 cm at x 36) with a 3 cm shoulder collar at x 33.5-34.3. Keyseat: 6 mm wide (P9, a light press fit), 3.5 mm deep, 25.6 mm long, on top of the shaft, centred at x 32. Key: steel parallel key 6 x 6 x 25 mm with round ends (DIN 6885 form A), long side along x, lying on a green 8 x 8 cm mat at x 27, y -13. Pulley: aluminium, 6 cm rim 1.2 cm wide plus a 3.6 cm boss 2.4 cm long (3.6 cm overall), 2 cm H7 bore with a 6 mm D10 keyway 6.05 mm wide and 2.8 mm deep (0.05 mm side clearance on the 6.00 mm key, 0.3 mm over it); started on the shaft end (front face at x 20.1), keyway turned 45 deg toward -y. Set screw: steel M6 x 1.0, 5 mm long, 3 mm hex socket, flat point, in the boss over the keyway, 1.2 cm from the front face, its top 0.2 mm below the boss surface and its point flush with the keyway roof, 0.3 mm clear of where the key will sit. Hex driver: 3 mm hex tip, 8 mm steel shank, 2 cm square orange handle, 4.6 cm long, 60 g, standing in the 1.2 cm hole of a brown rack block (3.6 x 3.6 x 2.2 cm) at x 26, y 13.
scoring: Score 0, latched, if the key falls below the bench top by 2 cm, or the pulley's rear face gets 2 mm past the front end of a key that sits in the keyseat but is not fully home (or cocked over 5 deg). Otherwise 0.25 for each step, counted only with every step before it: (1) key pressed home onto the keyseat floor (top 1.25 cm above the shaft axis, within 0.8 mm horizontally and 0.25 mm vertically of the seated pose, tilt under 3 deg, bearing on the depressed keyseat pad) and no gripper within 1 cm of it; (2) pulley over the key and against the shoulder (within 1.5 mm), no gripper within 1 cm, moving under 1 cm/s; (3) set screw tightened with the hex driver onto the seated key: its flat point bears on the key's top face and turning it further takes at least 0.4 N*m (a torque driver set to 0.4 N*m clicks without the screw moving); (4) hex driver out of the screw, let go and at rest on the bench, and the pulley gives no more than 0.2 mm when pulled off the shoulder with 20 N for 1 s (the pull is applied once the driver is down and both grippers have been 2 cm clear for 0.5 s; a pulley that lets go is pulled off the shoulder—the pull stops once slip passes 3 mm—and loses step 2). Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Scored at the last step.
reset_notes: Stand the driver back in its rack, back the set screw out until its point is flush with the keyway roof, pull the pulley back to the shaft end with its keyway 45 deg off the top, tap the key out and lay it on the mat.
fidelity: Rigid boxes. Pulley rides slide+turn joint (non-contact bore). Key in keyway: 0.05 mm by contact. Keyseat: 0.10 mm, 6 N press pad welded on bearing contact. Screw: 1 mm/turn joint; clamp force 4 N/um past live bearing contact on key; torque 1.2 mm x force; hold 0.3 x force (0.4 N*m sized to gripper). Hex engages pre-authored socket joint within 0.5 mm, 4 deg, 10 deg (tip-socket collision filtered). Pull test is a 20 N spring joint. Key 20 g (vs 7 g).
